Among the animals we hunted were the wild aurochs, the ancestor of all domestic cattle. The domestication of cows led to the use of oxen as draught animals that could help farmers plough fields.

programme.title: Animals That Changed History - Season 1
programme.desc: Throughout history, humans have surrounded themselves with animals. But there are two species that are our undeniable favourites. Every dog today was once a wolf - genetically speaking. Wolves and hominids met as early as 400,000 years ago. Ancient hunter-gatherers and wolves competed for the same prey, and used the same tracking techniques.

programme.title: Big is beautiful
programme.desc: The world is full of giants, huge creatures that fill us with awe and wonder. Some are gentle giants. Others are deadly hunters. There are different ways of defining ‘big’ - biggest in volume, or the biggest of their kind. But one thing is for sure, the huge animals of this world are fascinating, diverse and beautiful.

programme.title: Sharks of the Icy North
programme.desc: We mostly know the nimble predators from the depths of tropical seas. At the same time very little is known about the sharks of the icy North.

programme.title: Animals That Changed History - Season 1
programme.desc: For most of our history, people have fallen victim to crippling disease, and not had a clue where it came from. Despite our best efforts, we are vulnerable - not, perhaps, to lions, tigers, and bears - but more to the killers we can’t even see. In America during the early 1980s, a mysterious new disease claims the lives of 159 people, most of them gay men.

programme.title: Animals That Changed History - Season 1
programme.desc: As a species, we believe we are more than just animals. We are inspired to express ourselves through words, art, music, and scientific endeavours. Our ancestors painted animals on cave walls - usually large mammals, like bison and deer. Animals were out first artistic subject, our first inspiration.

programme.title: The Story of Europe
programme.desc: Europe's history has many dark sides, but its culture is more than a small gleam of hope, it radiates in many areas far out into the world. The old continent sets standards in art, literature and science. Starting with the ancient Greeks, Europe produces a number of smart and creative minds: from Aristotle to Michelangelo and Einstein, from Beethoven to the Beatles.

programme.title: The Story of Europe
programme.desc: Europe has been a battle concept for centuries: it often takes foreign enemies to weld the Europeans together. But for centuries, they are primarily fighting against themselves. It was not until the Enlightenment and the French Revolution of 1789 that a new idea of Europe emerged based on common values: freedom, equality and fraternalism.

programme.title: The Story of Europe
programme.desc: Europe has never experienced such a long period of peace and prosperity as after the Second World War. When the Iron Curtain falls in 1989, the dream of a Europe united in peace and freedom seems finally to become reality. But whether financial or refugee crisis - the European euphoria has disappeared, nationalists are on the rise again.

programme.title: Wild Sex
programme.desc: Sex is at the heart of everything. It’s the only real way of leaving a legacy - in the genes of the future. But there’s more than just the act - it’s the build up to it when wildlife shows its incredible diversity. It drives touching courtships and fierce battles. Hormones and sex drive are forces that shape behaviour and can change an animal’s purpose and persona. This is the story of how wild things get sexy.

programme.title: Wild Dolphins
programme.desc: In the waters surrounding New Zealand live a number of dolphin species - each of which has evolved unique strategies in their family pods to survive and thrive in the different habitats around these islands in the Pacific Ocean. On the east coast of the south island off the iconic Kaikoura peninsula, an underwater canyon pushes water seething with nutrients to the surface which provides a year round banquet for huge pods of dusky dolphins. These athletic and highly social dolphins spend their nights feeding out in the canyon, and in early morning they return closer to shore where they rest socialize and play. One of their favourite activities is the “seaweed game” where individuals pass pieces of seaweed to each other practicing fancy maneuvers where they’ll catch it on their tail, dorsal or pectoral fins. Down in the south west corner of New Zealand in the majestic landscape of Fiordland live the southern-most bottlenose dolphins. At almost 4 metres long these dolphins have adapted physically to the extreme winter conditions down here by growing bigger and fatter with extra insulating blubber and evolving stubbier beaks and shorter fins and tail flukes to reduce heat loss through their extremities. These fiords are different to the coastal environment in that freshwater sits on top of the denser seawater in a distinct layer, and is much colder than the saltwater and can prove lethal to the pods’ calves in winter, so every year the bottlenose dolphins make a short migration to the outer fiords where there is less freshwater to enable their calves to survive. In the water surrounding this volcano roam common dolphins - the nomads of the dolphin world. They are pelagic predators which mean they roam the open ocean searching for prey.

programme.desc: Having previously been dominated by the Empires of Russia, Germany and Austro-Hungary, many peoples of Eastern Europe had cherished hopes of gaining freedom after World War I.

programme.title: The End of the Ottomanns
programme.desc: At the end of WWI, the Treaty of Versailles and the Treaty of Sèvres stood for a new world order. This is where the victorious powers decided the Ottoman Empire was to be broken up.

programme.title: Gold for Kim - A Life for North Korea's Leader
programme.desc: North Korea is a country of stark contrasts. On the one hand, it presents real socialist stereotypes like cryptic messages from a frozen time loop, combined with shocking reports on shortages. On the other hand, polished Pyongyang lures with a futuristic skyline, flashy amusement parks and department stores with a range of goods equal to those in western consumer meccas.

programme.title: Signs of Evil - The Runes of the SS
programme.desc: The symbol of the SS, Hitler’s Schutzstaffel, stands for terror and the murder of millions. The penniless graphic artist Walter Heck was given the job of designing the jagged, rune-like characters in 1929. The “sig” rune was rooted deep in the ideological cosmos of the Nazis and their supporters. They saw themselves as the descendants of the Teutons and declared the runes to be humanity’s original Germanic script. The symbol was meant to unite Heinrich Himmler’s “Black Order.” But did it escape their notice that it was originally of Semitic origin? In October 1945, the Allies passed a law banning the Nazi Party and all associated organizations, including the SS. The young Federal Republic even forbade all Nazi symbols. This documentary tells the gripping story of the SS symbol, from the Middle Ages to the present day.

programme.title: Mata Hari - The Beautiful Spy
programme.desc: In February 1917 World War I is raging when Mata Hari is arrested in Paris and taken to the examining magistrate. Her very life is at stake: she is accused of high treason. The famous exotic dancer has come to represent beauty and the power of feminine seduction. The documentary Mata Hari - the Beautiful Spy tracks down the true story of this fascinating woman.

programme.title: The Child Crusades - Barefoot to the Promised Land
programme.desc: In Cologne in 1212 a boy named Nicholas captivated thousands of children between the ages of eight and fifteen with his fanatical speeches. They had been chosen, he said, to liberate Jerusalem. Likewise, in the French town of Cloyes a young shepherd gathered numerous children around him with the same proclamation.

programme.title: Forest of Heroes
programme.desc: From Lower Saxony and North Rhine Westphalia, from Osnabrück to Paderborn, one of Germany’s most beautiful forests extends for some 150 kilometers - the Teutoburg Forest. The low mountain range became famous due to the Varus Battle that took place in 9 AD. It was here that Hermann, or Arminius, the Cherusci Prince vanquished the Roman occupation army.

programme.title: The Battle for the Baltic Sea
programme.desc: It’s in spring 2008, when the telephone of the Archaeological State Office Schleswig-Holstein suddenly rings. The message archeologist Martin Segschneider receives makes him curious.

programme.title: Operation Peter Pan - The Secret War against Cuba
programme.desc: In 2016, a historic moment arrived when Barack Obama spoke in Cuba to the inhabitants of the island nation and promised a future together. For the first time in more than 50 years, an American president had entered the communist country and turned towards an erstwhile enemy. However, the US economic embargo against Cuba continues. It sanctions the socialist state – although the UN General Assembly recently again called it a violation of international law. Many Cubans are therefore sceptical about a new political future, despite the friendly words of the American President. Their distrust is deep. It is based on over fifty years of history and the policies of the United States towards their country. For years, the Cuban government has raised serious allegations against their big neighbour. The film "Operation Peter Pan" tracks these allegations.

programme.title: Monsters and Myths
programme.desc: Monsters have always been part of our nightmares and fairy tales. But where do they actually come from? How much of them is truth, how much is myth? Going to great lengths in this documentary, the filmmakers join scientists to explore a number of the best known sagas and legends in the world.

programme.title: World War A - When Aliens Attack
programme.desc: Scientists are already looking feverishly for evidence of extraterrestrial life. With the ExoMars mission, ESA will soon find life on Mars. If there are only tiny microbes, there could also be life in other places in the universe. But can life in space exist at all? The exobiologist Jean-Pierre de Vera collects microorganisms around the world and tests them in his Mars simulation laboratory. Can they survive under the deadly conditions of Mars? Researchers believe there are planets on which alien life can exist. In 1991 the Swiss astrophysicist Michel Mayor discovered the world's first exoplanet. Since then, about 3,000 planets have been detected outside our solar system. Heike Rauer from the German Aerospace Center is looking for habitable planets. Will she find a second earth? The European Southern Observatory is also searching for life in space, building the largest telescope in the world. In the next 20 years the E-ELT should be able to prove the existence of life on distant planets. How would extraterrestrials look? Some scientists suspect that they may well resemble us humans. Under other environmental conditions, alien life could also arise completely differently. It could be formed from methane and silicon. Different gravity would form alien bodies completely differently. Could extraterrestrials send us messages? At the SETI Institute in California, alien hunters like Seth Shostak are listening to signals from alien civilizations. But mere listening is no longer enough. Some SETI researchers now want to send messages to the aliens themselves. They hope to finally get an answer. But would that be a bad idea? Many scientists warn of the dangers of establishing contact. The former SETI researcher and science fiction author David Brin also fears that it could be a devastating mistake. With well-meant news we could end up attracting attention from hostile civilizations. Should we really tell them that we exist and where they can find us?

programme.title: UFOs and the Cold War
programme.desc: Pop culture is unthinkable without them, and so is the Cold War: UFO’s, those flying saucers allegedly bringing aliens to dominate the world.

programme.title: The Balkans in Flames
programme.desc: The documentary THE BALKANS IN FLAMES examines the disintegration of the former Socialist Federation of Yugoslavia.

programme.title: Hannibal: A March on Rome
programme.desc: Hannibal’s crossing of the Alps, one of the greatest military feats ever.

programme.title: Crime Scene Eulau - The Mystery of the 13 Skeletons
programme.desc: This documentary focuses on a spectacular discovery made in a quarry near the village of Eulau, not far from the central German town of Naumburg. Neolithic graves contained the skeletons of three women, two men and eight children, buried tenderly 4500 years ago, some affectionately entwined. In 2008, for the first time anywhere in the world, it was possible to perform a DNA analysis on the earliest evidence of the existence of a nuclear family. This was a sensation - but why did these people all die at the same time? Were they the victims of a violent crime? Who were they, and how did this terrible drama unfold? Archaeologists insist that these victims will not be forgotten, since these days it is possible to do far more than simply date and record such finds. Modern scientific methods have revolutionised archaeology, enabling us to discover how and why the family from Eulau in the German state of Sachsen-Anhalt died 4500 years ago. By enlisting the help of a CID profiler, archaeologists and anthropologists employ state-of-the-art analytical methods to investigate this Stone Age crime. In the process we discover key information about an era before recorded history which has previously been shrouded in mystery - and astonishing information about the composition of the population here also comes to light. It seems that the third millennium before Christ saw two major waves of migration, from Eastern and Western Europe, which determine the composition of the population here. In the middle of what is now Germany these two migratory movements met. Could this be the background to the mysterious murders of Eulau?

programme.title: Inside Hitler's Killing Machine
programme.desc: It took less than 10 years for Hitler to set up the concentration camps, many of which became centers for mass killing. programme.title: U.S. Marines in Vietnam

programme.title: War Machines

programme.title: World of Warships Clash of Titans

programme.title: Soviet Storm

Stalin promises to help Roosevelt, but the dropping of the Atomic bomb on Japan suddenly alters the calculus for the Allies. Despite the devastation, the Japanese military vows to fight on.

programme.title: 3 Days in the Life of Lt. Kravtsov

programme.title: Soviet Storm

programme.title: The Attackers

programme.title: Battlefields
programme.desc: August 26th, 1944, General de Gaulle has just returned to Paris. For the inhabitants of the capital, this is deliverance after four years of occupation. Discover what actually happened in Paris.

programme.title: WWII: The Road To Victory

programme.title: 3 Days in the Life of Lt. Kravtsov

programme.title: The Crusade in Europe

programme.title: WWII In Color: US Army Air Forces

programme.title: Unsealed: America's Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: Some people think everything is a conspiracy. Luckily for them, the FBI declassified decades' worth of government documents in April 2011, allowing people to gain more insight behind some of the most popular conspiracy theories. Each episode of this series investigates a compelling theory by opening these and other files. After acquiring new information, the show's team of specialists re-examines faulty assumptions, looks for inconsistencies and explores new leads in an attempt to get to the bottom of each case. Just make sure you have your tin foil handy when watching the show.

programme.title: Woodworkers Guild of America presented by CraftsyTV
programme.desc: In the episode the craftsman guides viewers through essential techniques and considerations for crafting cabinet doors with precision and efficiency. He begins by stressing the importance of wood selection, advising against woods with prominent grain patterns like oak, which are unsuitable for door frames. Instead, he recommends using straight-grained pieces from the edges of the wood or opting for materials like MDF, birch, or maple for paint-grade projects due to their smooth surfaces and availability in large sheets. The craftsman demonstrates how to prepare materials for construction, including ripping pieces for frames and face frames, and discusses the suitability of poplar for practice due to its affordability and ease of machining. When it comes to door panels, he explains the careful use of plywood and the importance of adjusting grooves precisely for optimal fit. He showcases the use of a dado head to create tenons that snugly fit into these grooves, ensuring strong and gap-free assembly. Techniques for creating specific door styles are highlighted, such as using half-lap joints adjusted on the table saw for flush fits. The craftsman emphasizes marking and consistent cuts to avoid errors, crucial for achieving perfect joints in door frame assembly. He demonstrates assembly steps and discusses adding decorative pegs for both aesthetic appeal and structural integrity, particularly useful for heavier doors like those with leaded glass panels. Throughout the episode, the craftsman underscores the use of templates for ensuring consistent shapes, particularly useful for cathedral-style doors. He employs a band saw and router table with double-sided tape to achieve precision in shaping components, emphasizing careful setup and sequential cuts for optimal woodworking results. Overall, the episode provides comprehensive guidance on wood selection, tool adjustment, joint creation, and assembly techniques, empowering woodworkers to create high-quality cabinet doors effectively.

programme.title: Woodworkers Guild of America presented by CraftsyTV
programme.desc: In the episode the craftsman guides viewers through essential techniques and considerations for crafting cabinet doors with precision and efficiency. He begins by stressing the importance of wood selection, advising against woods with prominent grain patterns like oak, which are unsuitable for door frames. Instead, he recommends using straight-grained pieces from the edges of the wood or opting for materials like MDF, birch, or maple for paint-grade projects due to their smooth surfaces and availability in large sheets. The craftsman demonstrates how to prepare materials for construction, including ripping pieces for frames and face frames, and discusses the suitability of poplar for practice due to its affordability and ease of machining. When it comes to door panels, he explains the careful use of plywood and the importance of adjusting grooves precisely for optimal fit. He showcases the use of a dado head to create tenons that snugly fit into these grooves, ensuring strong and gap-free assembly. Techniques for creating specific door styles are highlighted, such as using half-lap joints adjusted on the table saw for flush fits. The craftsman emphasizes marking and consistent cuts to avoid errors, crucial for achieving perfect joints in door frame assembly. He demonstrates assembly steps and discusses adding decorative pegs for both aesthetic appeal and structural integrity, particularly useful for heavier doors like those with leaded glass panels. Throughout the episode, the craftsman underscores the use of templates for ensuring consistent shapes, particularly useful for cathedral-style doors. He employs a band saw and router table with double-sided tape to achieve precision in shaping components, emphasizing careful setup and sequential cuts for optimal woodworking results. Overall, the episode provides comprehensive guidance on wood selection, tool adjustment, joint creation, and assembly techniques, empowering woodworkers to create high-quality cabinet doors effectively.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The remaining six bakers bring the old fashioned suet pudding bang up to date in the signature challenge, Mary Berry asks the bakers to produce 8 perfect religieuse, delicate choux buns filled with crème patissiere, and in the showstopper they must make three different types of puffed pastry.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It’s the quarter finals and just five bakers remain. The judges test the bakers with a signature challenge to produce a loaf using non traditional wheat flours, tested in the technical with a dacquoise recipe and pushed outside their comfort zone to create showstopping novelty vegetables cakes.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It's the Semi final and there are just four bakers left. This time it is the French round, and the challenges include savour canapes an opera cake and a Charlotte Royale. Whilst Mel travels to the Paris Opera House to discover where the dessert originated. Whose will hit the right note with the judges?

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It's the final of The Great British Baking Show! 13,000 applicants were narrowed down to 13 of Britain's best amateur bakers, and the 13 became three. There are just three final challenges standing between the three bakers and the title of WINNER of the Great British Baking Show.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: We catch up with last year's bakers, who have come a long way since their time in the tent. This programme looks back at the golden moments - and recurring nightmares - of the bakers dozen from last year, as they revisit their time in the tent and share their memories

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: As they enter the tent for the very first time, the baker’s first Signature Challenge is to make a swiss roll. The Technical Challenge is Mary’s recipe for a classic cherry cake. In the Showstopper. The bakers must make classic British cakes... in perfect miniature... all 36 of them...

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The remaining 11 bakers are tested on biscuits. The bakers must push themselves on flavour to create biscuits that go well with a cheese course. In the technical challenge Mary sets the bakers her recipe for Florentines. And the bakers are challenged to create three-dimensional biscuit scenes.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The remaining bakers brave bread and bake 12 perfect rye bread rolls in the signature challenge. In the technical challenge, Paul tells them to 'be patient' with his recipe for ciabatta loaves. Finally, the bakers are tasked to make a filled centrepiece loaf that will have an impact on a table

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It’s dessert week, the bakers must bake saucy puds - delicate sponges hiding a gooey saucy filling. For the technical challenge, Mary sets her tiramisu cake. For their final flourish, the bakers are challenged to bake incredible show-stopping baked alaskas made up of cake, meringue and ice cream

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The remaining bakers are facing pies and tarts. a signature custard tart that gives more than one of them a wobble. Paul sets the bakers mini pear pies in the technical challenge. Finally, the baker have just four hours to create a towering collection of pies from any pastry.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: For the signature challenge the bakers make yeast-leavened cakes, a tricky cross between cake and bread. Mary sets the technical challenge a Swedish princess torte and the showstopper is a two-tiered contemporary version of the traditional multi-layered Hungarian cake Dobos torte.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The remaining bakers make signature savoury parcels, ranging from pasties to samosas. Paul's technical challenge - kouign amann tests the bakers' technical ability and patience to create a yeasted pastry full of buttery sugary layers. Finally, the bakers make show-stopping eclairs creations

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It's the quarter-finals and the bakers make enriched sweet fruit loaves for their signature challenge. The technical challenge is a European treat filled with swirls of cinnamon and walnuts. And a show-stopper in which the bakers must make 36 show-stopping doughnuts of two different types.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The semi-finalists are challenged to make signature baklava. The technical challenge sees the bakers make German schichttorte cake which cooked under the grill. The show-stopper challenge raises the bar even higher. The final four bakers must bake nonstop to create two elegant entremets.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It's the final…just three challenges lie between them and the trophy. A signature challenge that requires the mastery of a classic pastry technique: a technical challenge with no recipe, and a show-stopper challenge that demands delivery of perfect sponge, caramel, choux pastry and petit four

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: Looking back over the incredible bakes of the last series, from Luis's amazing 3D biscuit scene, via the technically challenging schichttorte to Ian's binning of his baked alaska. We hear from the bakers, share their memories and catch up with what they have been doing since.

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: Sue Perkins hosts the first episode, in which cricketer Michael Vaughan, James Bond and Downton Abbey actress Samantha Bond, Harry Potter actress Bonnie Wright and broadcaster Johnny Vaughan enter the tent. Who will walk away with the Star Baker Apron?

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: Sue Perkins hands over the baton to Jo Brand to support the next four celebrity bakers. This time the battle is between Desert Island Discs' Kirsty Young, singer and actress Jane Horrocks, Olympic gold-medal winning long jumper Greg Rutherford and ice skating's Mr Nasty, Jason Gardiner

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: Omid Djalili this time and those facing the judges are Olivier award-winning singer Michael Ball, broadcaster and co-founder of Comic Relief Emma Freud, singer and presenter Jamelia and Olympic gold-medallist Victoria Pendleton. But only one can win the Star Baker apron

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: It is Ed Byrne's turn to take up the baking baton and support the four celebrities as they face their three challenges in the tent. The bakers must make pizzas for their signature challenge, eccles cakes in the technical challenge and showstopping tiered cakes that represent sporting equipment.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo is joined by Roisin Conaty, Paul Rankin and Gregg Wallace to discuss the 12 new bakers and their bakes. What do the panel think of the bakers' Swiss roll? And how did they fare with Mary Berry's cherry cake? Whose 36 miniature cakes stopped the show? Plus lots of 'exclusive' footage from the tent.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo Brand is joined by three celebrity fans - chef Monica Galetti, actress Lisa Faulkner and comedian Charlie Baker to discuss the 11 bakers and their biscuit bakes. Jo looks at the good, bad and the soggy bottomed, with chat, unseen footage and an interview with the week’s eliminated.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo and her panel of celebrity fans: Julian Clary, Richard Coles and Rosemary Shrager, discuss the ten bakers and the bread they have baked. What do the panel think of the bakers' rye rolls? How did they fare with the technical challenge - ciabatta? And whose filled centrepiece loaf stood out?

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo Brand and three celebrity fans highlights from the tent, with chat, unseen footage and an interview with the week's eliminated baker. Comedian Roisin Conaty, chef Glynn Purnell and former contestant Howard Middleton look back at one of the most sensational episodes of Baking Show yet.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: It is pies and tarts week in the tent, so Jo and her panel of celebrity fans: Chef Michel Roux Jr, comedian Shappi Khorsandi and former home secretary Alan Johnson continue the theme in the An Extra Slice studio, looking at audience bakes and viewer photos - the good, the bad and the disastrous.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: It is European cake week in the tent, so Jo and her panel of fans celebrate them by tasting audience bakes and looking at viewer photos of bakes from home - the triumphs and the tragedies. Actress Fay Ripley, comedian Romesh Ranganathan and chef Richard Corrigan are Jo Brand's guests in the studio

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: It is pastries week in the tent, which means Jo Brand and her panel of celebrity fans are celebrating anything and everything to do with pastry. In the studio, the panel looks at bakes brought in by the audience and viewer photos of their bakes from home - the delectable and the downright disastrous.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo Brand is joined by Hairy Biker Dave Myers, author Marian Keyes and comedian Hal Cruttenden to look back at advanced dough week. Who do they think shone making doughnuts in the show-stopper? And who do they think will make the final three and eventually be crowned winner?

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo Brand is joined by chef Tom Aikens, actress Fay Ripley and comedian Josh Widdicombe. What do the panel have to say about the bakers' signature baklavas? How did the bakers cope with making entremets for the show-stopper? The panel also give their best guesses at who will be crowned winner.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo Brand looks back at the final with Paul Hollywood, Mary Berry and all of the year's bakers, including the newly-crowned Champion. Jo interviews this year's champion, the two runners-up and is joined by all of this year's bakers. Plus, there’s unseen footage and a look at viewer and audience bakes

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: 12 new bakers head for the Baking Show tent. Judges Mary Berry and Paul Hollywood have created 3 challenges that will test their baking prowess. Starting with cake week, the bakers make a madeira cake, are tested with a frosted walnut cake and try to impress with a black forest gateau showstopper.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: This week the remaining bakers tackle biscuits. The signature challenge is to create 24 biscotti. Paul chooses the technical challenge, arlettes, a French reverse puff pastry biscuit. And finally, the show-stopper is to build an edible biscuit box filled with 36 biscuits of a different flavour

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The ten remaining bakers must make quick breads – they have an hour and a half to get creative with their flavours. Paul sets baguettes as the technical challenge. A seemingly simple recipe or is it? For their show-stopper, the bakers must make edible 3D bread sculptures

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: For the nine bakers left, it's time to tackle desserts. The signature challenge comes in the form of a French classic - creme brulee. Mary picks the technical challenge - the spanische windtorte from Austria. Three baked cheesecakes make up the final show-stopper challenge

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The remaining bakers must bake without sugar, gluten or dairy. The bakers create a variety of sugar-free cakes and use honey, agave syrup and fruit. Paul picks the technical challenge, gluten-free pittas. For their show-stopper, the bakers must make dairy-free ice cream rolls.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The bakers prove their skill with pastry by making frangipane tarts for their signature challenge. The technical challenge is a cheese-filled pastry from Cyprus - the flaouna. The show-stopper is the classic 70s canape, vol-au-vents: bitesize puff pastry stuffed with tasty fillings

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The bakers go back to the Victorian era and make a dinner table staple, the game pie. The bakers then make a perfect fruit cake that resembles a tennis court. For the show-stopper, the bakers make charlotte russe, a dessert with a silky bavarois centre surrounded by sponge fingers and topped with jelly

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: No series of Baking Show would be complete without testing the bakers on patisserie, and what better time to do it than the quarter-finals? The five remaining bakers must work their way through childhood favourites and delicate french fancies to a mountainous choux pastry masterpiece.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It's the semi-finals and the remaining bakers must get to grips with chocolate. They revisit their old friend pastry for a chocolate tart signature, Mary sets a technical challenge to make a chocolate souffle. And the bakers create spectacular chocolate centrepieces for their showstopper.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: Three finalists and three final challenges. The bakers create delicious filled iced buns in the signature. The technical requires them to conquer something they’ve all struggled with, and for their showstopper, they make a classic British cake. Who will hold their nerve and be crowned the winner

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The bakers from Series 6 return to the tent for a special look back. A lot has happened in the year since they hung up their aprons. They share their memories, relive their highlights of the series and reveal what they are up to now.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Kicking off the series, Jo and her panel of Celebrity fans will give us their take on the 12 new bakers. Will they go mad for the bakers' madeira cake? How do they think the dozen coped with their first technical bake - Mary's frosted walnut cake? Whose black forest gateau show-stopper stopped the show?

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: It's biscuit week, so Jo and her celebrity guests celebrate all sorts of biscuits, tasting audience attempts at cookies and crackers and looking at viewer photos of their bakes from home. They’ll also be unseen footage from the tent and chat with the eliminated baker.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: It's bread week, so Jo and guests Deborah Meaden, Richard Bertinet and Josh Widdicombe cast their eyes over the home-baked breads brought in by the studio audience. They also look through photos of viewers' home baking efforts and chat to the eliminated baker.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Joining host Jo Brand are three celebrity fans - Glynn Purnell, Liza Tarbuck and Henning Wehn - who dissect this week's action from the Bake Off tent. As well as lots of witty chat and exclusive footage from the tent and there's an interview with the latest baker to leave.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Judy Murray, Michael Caines and Hal Cruttenden join Jo Brand to give their take on this week's sugar- and gluten-free Bake Off shenanigans.Jo and her guests also taste bakes brought in by the audience, also look at photos of viewer bakes from home - the good, the bad and the downright catastrophic

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: The first brave celebrities to enter the Bake Off Tent are four of the most iconic figures in British entertainment - Joanna Lumley, Jennifer Saunders, Lulu, and Dame Edna Everage - who has come out retirement especially for Comic Relief. They must take on three challenges set by Mary and Paul

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: Mel Giedroyc welcomes four more celebrities into the tent to test out their baking expertise. They are Gok Wan, Jonathan Ross, Abbey Clancy and Zoe Sugg - also known as internet sensation Zoella. Who will impress legendary cookery writer Mary Berry and acclaimed master baker Paul Hollywood?

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: In the third episode Jo Brand welcomes four more celebrities into the tent to lay bare their baking skills. They are David Mitchell, Michael Sheen, Radio 1 DJ Jameela Jamil and Sarah Brown. Tensions are high and confusion is rife, but who will impress and who will miss the mark?

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: Ed Byrne welcomes Victoria Wood, Alexa Chung, Chris Moyles and Kayvan Novak to the tent. They face three tricky challenges set by Mary and Paul.Who will demonstrate baking brilliance and be crowned star baker?

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Joining host Jo Brand in the An Extra Slice studio are three celebrity fans - Marcus Wareing, Marian Keyes and Rob Beckett - all eager to chew over pastry week in the tent.Jo and her guests taste audience bakes and look at viewer photos of their home bakes - from tantalising tarts to pitiful pastries.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: It is week seven and just six bakers remain. Joining host Jo Brand in the An Extra Slice studio are three celebrity Bake Off fans - Michel Roux Jnr, David Baddiel and historian Ruth Goodman - eager to chew over the latest goings-on in the tent. An Extra Slice – perfect if you can’t resist a second helping.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Sarah Millican stands in and is joined by Gregg Wallace, Joe Lycett and pastry chef Cherish Finden to dissect the events in the tent, with unseen footage and an interview with eliminated baker. They also taste bakes brought in by the studio audience and look at viewer photos of their bakes from home

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo Brand is joined by celebrity fans - Danny Baker, Josh Widdicombe and Tom Aikens - to dissect how the bakers tackled chocolate. As well as unseen footage Jo and the panel taste bakes by the studio audience and look at photos viewers home bakes. Jo interviews the last baker to leave before the final

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo Brand is joined in the studio by Paul Hollywood and Mary Berry to get their take on the nerve-wracking final bakes and how and why they chose their eventual winner. Jo will interview the champion, the two runners-up and will be joined by all of this year's bakers. Plus a look at the audience bakes too.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The competition begins with a British classic and Mary's technical challenge - a popular cake with a fatless sponge and tricky chocolate work. Finally, the bakers show the judges what they can do with their showstopper. One baker will be crowned star baker, one contestant will be leaving the tent.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It’s biscuit week and the bakers signature challenge is to make 24 identical decorated biscuits. The technical challenge requires perfect piping to avoid a crumbling whirl. The showstopper requires precision baking to build a biscuit structure that reveals a little more about each of the bakers

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It’s bread week, and Paul Hollywood sets the challenges. First up is the signature challenge - a sweet dough with a twist. The technical challenge has only a basic set of instructions and ingredients. And the final challenge requires three different flours to create a showstopper centrepiece.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The bakers really have to rise to the occasion for batter week. The signature challenge is a British favourite. The technical challenge requires a steady hand to master its intricacies. And finally, there is a show-stopper as the bakers are challenged to do their version of a Spanish classic.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It is Pastry Week and the remaining bakers face a Danish style breakfast staple. In the technical challenge, the bakers have limited time and instructions to bake a classic British tart. And in the showstopper, a fine pastry which is notoriously difficult to make and even trickier to bake.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It's Botanical Week with three challenges inspired by nature. The signature challenge demands sharp citrus flavours and perfect peaks. There’s a leafy technical challenge set by Mr Hollywood. And, finally, the botanical showstopper is a three tier elaborately decorated cake.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: Dessert Week - three sweet challenges and for starters the bakers face a sweetly filled signature challenge. The technical challenge layers on the pressure as the bakers are tested on a tricky French dessert. And finally there is a multi-bake mini-showstopper that is a bit of a mousse marathon.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: Tudor Week and three challenges that embrace a time when impressive centre pieces were Tudor showstoppers. The signature is a Tudor classic - pies. In the technical challenge, the bakers face a rather unusual Tudor biscuit. And a showstopper that is a spectacle of marzipan.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It’s the semi-final, and Patisserie Week. In the signature challenge, the bakers have to achieve perfect lamination for a difficult French pastry. In the technical challenge, the bakers' are tested with a yeast-based cake. The show-stopper is a multiple mini-cake bake.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It’s the final, and the tent plays host to three Royal challenges to impress the Queen. The signature challenge sees a return to meringues. For the technical challenge, the bakers have only one recipe instruction. Then the bakers' face their last show-stopper. Who will be crowned champion?

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Each week, host Jo Brand chats to a panel of celebrity fans, looking at all the shenanigans in the tent. Jo shines a spotlight on the best, the worst and the 'must try harder next time' bakes from the latest episode, with chat and an interview with the baker who left the tent that week.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: This week, Jo Brand is joined by comedian Josh Widdicombe and chef Rosemary Shrager to dissect the latest goings-on, with unseen footage and an interview with the latest baker to leave the tent. Jo and her guests celebrate biscuit week by tasting audience attempts at gingerbread and garibaldis.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Host Jo Brand is joined by three celebrity fans who give their take on the remaining ten bakers and their bakes. Jo and her guests also cast their eyes over the baked bread brought in by the studio audience and look at viewer photos of their bakes from home, be they triumphs or heroic fails.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Joining host Jo Brand in the An Extra Slice studio are former shadow chancellor Ed Balls, chef Monica Galetti and comedian Henning Wehn. As well as dissecting this week's goings on in the tent, Jo interviews the latest baker to leave, reveals more exclusive footage and tastes the audience home bakes

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Host Jo Brand is joined by three celebrity guests, including renowned chef Michel Roux Jr, giving their take on this week's shenanigans. Along with chat and unseen footage, Jo interviews the latest baker to leave the tent and tastes the audience bakes – the good and the bad!

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Joining host Jo Brand in the studio are three celebrity fans including Danny Baker, all eager to chew over the latest goings on in the tent. There is unseen footage, chat about the latest baking shenanigans and an interview with the latest baker to leave.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Joining host Jo Brand to dissect the latest goings on are - double Olympic silver medalist Rebecca James, Crème de la Crème judge Cherish Finden and comedian Chris Addison. Jo will also taste the desserts the studio audience have brought along and look at pictures of viewers bakes from home.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo Brand hosts and is joined by celebrity fans to discuss Tudor week. There is unseen footage and an interview with the latest baker to leave. The panel taste bakes brought in by the studio audience and look at viewer photos of their bakes from home - the delicacies and the calamities.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: It is the semi-finals in the tent. Jo Brand hosts and is joined by three celebrity fans, including reigning Bake Off champion Nadiya Hussain and leader of the Scottish Conservative & Unionist Party Ruth Davidson. Which baker will the panel tip to be crowned the Champion?

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo Brand is joined in the studio by Mary Berry to get her take on the final bakes and why she and Paul chose their eventual champion. Jo interviews the year's winner as well as the two runners-up, and she is also joined by the rest of the year's bakers, as well as Sarah Millican and Hal Cruttenden

programme.title: The Great Pottery Throw Down
programme.desc: Judges Keith Brymer Jones and Rich Miller set a birthday tea set challenge and their surprise second challenge sees the potters making handleless milk jugs that must survive the bucket of doom. Who will be named potter of the week, and who will be first to leave the pottery?

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: Mel Giedroyc hosts featuring Jason Manford, Maddy Hill, David James and Samantha Cameron. contestants face three challenges - making canapes using rough puff pastry, preparing a Paris-Brest, a French dessert, and finally, creating a 3D cake in the shape of a sporting trophy.

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: The bakers on the starting line are former Labour politician Ed Balls, writer and presenter Victoria Coren Mitchell, sports commentator Chris Kamara and singer and actress Kimberley Walsh. Who will bag the coveted title of star baker?

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: The celebrities taking up the baking baton this time are ex-Spice Girl Geri Horner, BBC world affairs editor John Simpson, footballer and pundit Jermaine Jenas and 1990s pop sensation Louise Redknapp.Who will crumble under the pressure and who will triumph to take home the title of Star Baker?

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: The celebrities taking up the baking baton this time are actor Alison Steadman, comedian Ade Edmondson, singer Will Young and actor and comedian Morgana Robinson. Which of the bakes will measure up to the exacting standards of the judges and win them the coveted Star Baker apron?

programme.title: The Great Pottery Throw Down
programme.desc: It’s the second week in the pottery and all is not as it seems as the remaining potters hand build a keepsake box with a disguised lid, and face a surprise blindfold challenge. Judges Rich Miller and Keith Brymer Jones must decide who is potter of the week and who will leave the pottery.

programme.title: The Great Pottery Throw Down
programme.desc: It’s Retro Week in the pottery and host Siobhán McSweeney takes the ten remaining potters back in time as they create a trio of flying birds. And judges Keith Brymer Jones and Rich Miller set an old fashioned hot water bottle surprise challenge. Who will be potter of the week and who will be heading home?

programme.title: The Great Pottery Throw Down
programme.desc: It’s Raku week in the pottery, as the potters throw a pair of hanging planters to impress judges Rich Miller and Keith Brymer Jones. In the spot test, guest judge, ceramic artist and series two semi-finalist Freya Bramble-Carter returns to the pottery to set a challenge with a decorative flourish.

programme.title: The Great Pottery Throw Down
programme.desc: Host Siobhán McSweeney takes the eight remaining potters up on the roof as they create gargoyles. And guest judge Gabriel Nichols, from William Blyth Roof Tiles, sets them the challenge of making a chimney pot. Who is potter of the week and who will be heading home.

programme.title: The Great Pottery Throw Down
programme.desc: It’s an illuminating week in the pottery as the potters make a table light with a continuous, embossed scene. And the second challenge surprise guest judge, Fashion and Lifestyle Designer, Henry Holland really tests their decadent design skills.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Drill Charging Station
programme.desc: Back in 2010 I built a Drill Charging Station to show off a new joinery gadget. It was really simple and didn't quite have a feature set outside of being two shelves on the wall. So only eight short years later I finally decided to build a proper Drill Charging Station, made from Baltic Birch plywood featuring all the storage I need for 5 drills, two chargers, and all of my bits and accessories.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: DIY Kids School Desk - Quick - Easy - Inexpensive!
programme.desc: A one-day build using 1/4 sheet of plywood and a 2x4.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Knock Down Trestle Table Part 1
programme.desc: The table is a trestle design which keeps the legs out of the way and gives us plenty of overhang. The joinery is all mortise and tenon including some cool double wedged mortise and tenon joints. I even added extra supports in the middle of the table that will not only support the top but should also help keep the table top flat over time.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Woven Panel Rolling Hamper Part 2
programme.desc: The hamper is assembled, hinges are added, casters are attached, finish is applied, and snaps are installed on the cotton bags.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Tricked Out Bandsaws Featuring Carter Products
programme.desc: The bandsaw is one of my favorite tools and if you treat it well, it will quickly become one of your favorites as well. While most modern bandsaws come with decent components, to begin with, there are companies like Carter Products who make high-quality after-market add-ons that can make your bandsaw better performing and easier to adjust. One of the best upgrades you can do is replacing the guide

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Cutting Thin Strips at the Table Saw
programme.desc: Resawing thin stock and cutting thin strips is typically the domain of the bandsaw. And while I consider the bandsaw to be an essential shop tool, not everyone has one. So it's probably worth considering an alternative option that kills two birds with one stone: utilizing a more common tool that results in a smoother cut.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Protecting Outdoor Furniture with Epoxy Feet
programme.desc: Mother Nature always wins. So when you make outdoor furniture you have two choices: commit to a regular maintenance schedule or come to terms with the weathered gray look. An easy thing you can do to help the cause is to prevent moisture from entering into the legs. This simple trick requires nothing more than epoxy and masking tape.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Trestle Table Part 2
programme.desc: Now that the leg pieces are cut to their rough shape, we need to focus on blending the parts using an assortment of tools including a router, a ball mill, and a cabinet-maker’s rasp. You’ll notice that much of the sculpting work is done before the glueup. I find it much easier to work on these parts in smaller pieces rather than trying to work the entire finished leg at once.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: 60 Seconds to Sharp

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: You Don't Need Breadboard Ends - Ask TWW
programme.desc: You don't need breadboard ends - and that's why.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Urea Resin Woodworking Glues
programme.desc: We take a look at urea resin woodworking glues. These glues definitely have their advantages: low water content, gap-filling, long open time, and rigid glue lines just to name a few. But keep in mind the one big disadvantage: safety. These glues are pretty nasty and you might be best served considering other options. But with proper precautions, this glue can be a nice addition to your shop.

programme.desc: The guys over at VerySuperCool Tools recently gave me an opportunity to test out one of their new products: an after-market fence system. programme.title: GLORY Kickboxing
programme.desc: GLORY Kickboxing’s Summer of GLORY concluded with a massive event from the Johan Cruijff Arena in Amsterdam. In the night’s headliner, heavyweight champion Rico Verhoeven took on Brazilian challenger Guto Inocente. Verhoeven had defended his belt seven straight times since capturing the title in 2014. His winning streak inside the GLORY ring stood at 16. Inocente looked to dethrone the world’s top-ranked heavyweight riding the momentum of wins over Benjamin Adegbuyi, D’Angelo Marshall and Hesdy Gerges. Gold was also on the line in the co-main event, as longtime featherweight titleholder Robin van Roosmalen rematched interim champion Petchpanomrung Kiatmookao. The pair met previously at GLORY 41 — also in van Roosmalen’s home country of Holland — with the Dutchman taking home a controversial, majority-decision victory.
